result_text:
The mock-folder rule now matches any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock`, whatever follows. The new tests and the existing `SourceFileFilterTest` pass in the `codeanalyzer` module.

**Change:** In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/TestConventions.java`, I replaced the two old mock patterns (`.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`) with one pattern: `(.*/)?(__)?mock[^/]*/.*`.

- `[^/]*` covers any punctuation or non-ASCII characters in the rest of the folder name, and also allows a bare `mock/` folder, which the old pattern missed.
- The leading `(.*/)?` lets the folder sit at the root as well as at any depth.
- Backslash paths already work, because `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` tries the normalised forms of the path.
- `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` still match, and the `mocks` rule on line 82 is untouched.

**Tests:** I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/TestConventionsTest.java` with three cases. They cover the new folder names, the folders that were already test code, and the non-matches (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

Nothing is committed.
